For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). 3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to a substantive (not merely evidence-gathering) intervention? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

319	CASE OD2-DEV-MISLEAD (MISLEAD, technical): Checkout payment failures after the v4.12 release
320	Setting: Fernhollow Outfitters is a fictional online outdoor-gear retailer. Its checkout service, checkout-api (16 pods), sends card payments to an external gateway, Quillmark Payments, using API credentials. Since 3 March, roughly one payment attempt in 27 has failed, and the failures come and go. A new checkout release (v4.12) went out that morning, and a spring promotion started the same day. Engineering wants to roll the release back, and Finance wants a revenue-impact figure for the board.
321	Presenting request: The Head of Engineering asks: what is causing the intermittent payment failures since 3 March, should we approve the full rollback of checkout-api v4.12, and what should we do now?
322	INITIAL EVIDENCE
323	E1 [stage S1] Incident ticket INC-4471, checkout on-call (system-record): INC-4471 opened 3 March 11:20 by paging alert checkout_payment_failure_rate (rule: 30-minute failure rate at least 2% AND at least 40 failed attempts). Daily payment-attempt failure rate, checkout-api: 28 Feb 0.4%, 1 Mar 0.4%, 2 Mar 0.5%, 3 Mar 3.4%, 4 Mar 3.9%, 5 Mar 3.6%, 6 Mar 3.8%. All new failures carry error code PAYMENT_UPSTREAM_REJECTED. On-call summary: 'Intermittent. A customer fails, retries a few minutes later, often succeeds.' No pod restarts and no gateway timeouts recorded.
324	E2 [stage S1] Email from Dara Okonjo, Engineering Manager, Checkout, 6 March (manager-account): Subject: INC-4471, we know what this is. v4.12 shipped 3 March at 10:40 and the alert fired forty minutes later. The failure rate went from half a percent to nearly four overnight and has stayed there. v4.12 replaced our gateway HTTP client and connection-pool settings, which is exactly the code path that's failing. Quillmark's status page is green, so it isn't them. I want approval to roll the whole fleet back to v4.11 tonight and freeze checkout releases until we've rewritten the client. Dara
325	E3 [stage S1] Release notes, checkout-api v4.12 (CHG-2214) (change-record): checkout-api v4.12, deployed 3 March 10:40, CHG-2214, approved by Engineering CAB. Changes: (1) Gateway client moved to a new HTTP library; connection pool size raised from 50 to 64. (2) Error handling: every non-2xx response from the payment gateway now maps to one code, PAYMENT_UPSTREAM_REJECTED. The raw upstream status is no longer logged at INFO level. The customer message is unchanged: 'Your card was declined. Please try another card or try again.' (3) Security: partial card numbers previously written to debug logs are now masked, closing audit finding SEC-2291 (remediation deadline 13 March). A rollback to v4.11 reverts all three changes.
326	E4 [stage S1] Quillmark Payments status page capture and support ticket TS-90412 (vendor-account): Quillmark status page, captured 6 March 08:00: 'All systems operational' for Authorisation API, Search API and Merchant Dashboard on every day from 1 to 6 March; no incidents posted. Support ticket TS-90412, Quillmark reply of 5 March: 'We see no platform-wide incidents during the period. Our records show your requests are reaching us. Please review your integration and confirm you are handling all documented response codes.'
327	E5 [stage S1] Email from Priya Halvorsen, CFO, 6 March (leadership-account): Gross online revenue for the week to 6 March is down 9% on the prior week. The prior week did include the final days of Winter Clearance, which ended 1 March, and Spring Trail Sale launched on 3 March, but I'm clear in my mind that the checkout failures are what cost us. I need a figure for the board pack on Monday, and I expect us to restate the Q1 forecast on the back of it.
328	E6 [stage S1] Customer Care lead Tomasz Reyes, notes for INC-4471 bridge call, 5 March (staff-account): 238 customer contacts since 3 March about declined cards. Most say the decline came 'out of nowhere' and that a retry a few minutes later worked. Eleven customers phoned their bank. In nine of those cases the bank said it had no record of any authorisation attempt at the time of the failure. Agents have been advising customers to try a different card.
329	CATALOGUE (full contents)
330	C1 [stage S1] Canary rollback test results, CHG-2231, 5 March 12:00–18:00 - Checkout platform team (change-record): CHG-2231 canary, 5 March 12:00–18:00. 8 of 16 checkout-api pods rolled back to v4.11; the load balancer split traffic evenly. Results: v4.11 pods had 9,412 payment attempts with 351 failures (3.7%). v4.12 pods had 9,388 attempts with 338 failures (3.6%). v4.11 pods still log the raw gateway status. Of their 351 failures, 341 were HTTP 429 'Too Many Requests' and 10 were HTTP 402 card declines. Connection-pool saturation was 0% on both versions. The canary was reverted at 18:05 because v4.11 lacks the SEC-2291 card-number masking.
331	C2 [stage S1] checkout-api pod resource and connection-pool metrics, 1–6 March - Platform monitoring (telemetry): checkout-api, 16 pods, 1–6 March. CPU utilisation 22–41% at daily peaks, with no change after 3 March. Memory flat at about 1.1 GB per pod. Gateway connection-pool utilisation peaked at 31% (pool size 64 after v4.12, 50 before). p99 gateway call latency was 430 ms before the release and 410 ms after. Zero socket timeouts and zero connection-refused errors in the period. No autoscaling events.
332	C3 [stage S1] Per-minute payment failure counts, 3–6 March - Checkout analytics (telemetry): Per-minute failed payment attempts, 3–6 March. The first cluster was 3 March 09:00–09:03 (14 failures out of 61 attempts), followed by clusters at 09:15, 09:30, 09:45, 10:00, 10:15 and 10:30. All of these came before the 10:40 deploy, and morning volume stayed below the alert's minimum count until 11:20. Across 3–6 March, 93% of failures fall in minutes :00–:03, :15–:18, :30–:33 and :45–:48 between 09:00 and 21:00. Outside those minutes the failure rate is 0.4%. No clusters overnight. On 6 March 13:00–15:00, during a scheduled finance ERP maintenance window, no clusters occurred. They resumed at 15:00.
333	C4 [stage S1] Quillmark API usage report for credential fernhollow-prod-01, 1–6 March - Quillmark account team (vendor-account): Prepared 6 March. Credential fernhollow-prod-01. Rate limit: 300 requests/minute per credential, all endpoints combined. 1–2 March: /v2/payments peaked at 52/min; /v2/transactions/search near zero in the daytime, with one nightly run at 02:00 (about 1,900 calls over 9 minutes). From 3 March 09:00: /v2/transactions/search bursts of 360–430/min in the first 3–4 minutes of each quarter hour, 09:00–21:00, user-agent 'settle-recon/2.3'. /v2/payments steady at 30–58/min. HTTP 429 responses: 0 on 1–2 March; 4,980–6,310 per day on 3–6 March, all within burst minutes, header X-RateLimit-Scope: credential. Issuer declines steady at 0.3–0.4% of payments. Temporary limit increases take 3–5 business days and are chargeable.

Several customers mention the sale price as their reason for persisting.
339	C10 [stage S1] Peer review record for the v4.12 gateway client change (PR #1187) - Source control system (document): PR #1187, merged 2 March. rulings.explanation: The key's case for 'premature' rests on A3 depending on R4, which is not yet established. But A3 does not just say the incident contributed to the fall. It tells the board the incident caused the whole 9% and restates the Q1 forecast on that basis. The initial file already caps how much the incident could explain. E1 puts the extra failure rate at about 3.3–3.5 percentage points of attempts, and E1 and E6 say retries a few minutes later often succeed. Even if no failed customer ever retried, the incident could not account for a 9% revenue fall. If C6 is read, the rise in sessions combined with lower conversion and lower order value (1.24 × 2.5/3.1 × 68/74 ≈ 0.92) explains roughly an 8% fall without the incident. The order-value drop alone accounts for about 8%, and payment failures cannot cause that. C9 adds that only 6 of 50 sampled customers abandoned. So confirming that the incident contributed something would still not make A3's claim right. Putting that claim to the board and restating the forecast on it would misreport to leadership and hide the real drivers: the mix of new display-ad traffic and lower order value. That fits 'harmful' (worsens outcomes, suppresses information). 'Premature' also stays defensible under the item's own framing, because the authoring notes and the R4 edge treat A3 as hinging on R4. Both answers can be defended.

Keep the key as 'premature'. (Alternatively, keep A3 as written, change the key to 'harmful', and give the magnitude bound from E1 and C6 as the rationale.)
